question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x+y, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expected value of $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x+y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+xy]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {1}^{2}+1\cdot y-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}+y, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot (\frac{1}{2}+y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{y}{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{3})-0 \\  & =\frac{7}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$
